item.title: OpenAI unveils a 'Control Room' safety feature that shuts down AI agents from going rogue in 35 seconds
item.description: OpenAI said Control Room will connect every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. It will work together with its misalignment monitoring systems.
item.content:encoded:
OpenAI has introduced Control Room, a feature that halts any artificial intelligence (AI) output that raises safety or security concerns within 35 seconds, the company said in a blog post.

On the need for Control Room, the blog post said, “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed. To solve this, we built Control Room.”

Control Room will be a central system to track model workloads across the research infrastructure of OpenAI.

OpenAI said Control Room will connect every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. It will work together with its misalignment monitoring systems

The Control Room will be integrating a few systems: the workload, the inference engine and the centralised control room service.

The workload is the job being run, such as a reinforcement learning experiment, an evaluation, a high-volume sampling or data processing job. The inference engine is the key of any AI model. The Control Room service tracks jobs and controls whether they are allowed to continue generating model output.

The blog post noted that engines check with the Control Room service before fulfilling a request. If a job has been stopped, the service denies the request, preventing further output.

OpenAI said it runs continuous checks to detect unauthorised or modified inference engine implementations that may bypass Control Room.

“We additionally run continual agentic and programmatic sweeps to check that users are not accidentally or maliciously launching rogue engine implementations with Control Room unimplemented or disabled,” it noted.

OpenAI said it will continue to strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside its investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 10, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From Neha Nagar's debut book to tech leaders and startup founders that saw their careers derailed by personal scandals, YourStory brings you this and other latest developments across sectors.

Featured stories

Neha Nagar’s debut book aims to make personal finance accessible

Finance educator and content creator Neha Nagar has launched her debut book, Simple Money Serious Wealth: How to Turn Ordinary Income into Extraordinary Net Worth, to help readers make informed financial decisions and manage their money better.

Published on October 24, the book sold over 3,000 copies within its first 24 hours, according to a post on her Instagram account. Nagar, who has over a decade of experience in finance and seven years in content creation, says she decided to write the book after recognising that while people have access to financial information, many lack a structured approach to managing their money.

Nagar believes financial literacy in India still faces challenges, including the absence of personal finance education in schools, reluctance to discuss money within households, and the overwhelming amount of information available on social media.

Recognised by Hurun India as the country's most-followed female personal finance influencer in 2025, she wants the book to help readers build financial plans, understand investment options and make decisions suited to their needs. Her goal is to help people realise that financial independence is not just about how much they earn, but how confidently they manage their money.

Read more

Five tech and startup leaders whose personal controversies affected their careers

From India to Silicon Valley, several prominent technology and startup leaders have faced career setbacks following controversies involving personal relationships or workplace conduct. YourStory looks at five such cases, including former Infosys executive Phaneesh Murthy, who was dismissed as iGate CEO in 2013 following an investigation into his relationship with a subordinate, and The Viral Fever (TVF) founder Arunabh Kumar, who stepped down as CEO in 2017 after sexual harassment allegations surfaced. Kumar denied the allegations and was acquitted by a Mumbai court in 2022.

The list also includes former Intel CEO Brian Krzanich, who resigned in 2018 after the company found that his consensual relationship with an employee violated its non-fraternisation policy; former Google executive Andy Rubin, whose exit from the company came under scrutiny following reports of a sexual misconduct complaint and a $90 million exit package; and former HP CEO Mark Hurd, who resigned in 2010 after an investigation found violations of the company's business conduct standards. The report examines how the circumstances and outcomes differed across these cases.

Read more

Other news

IIT Madras, Gauhati University researchers develop new method to identify monsoon onset at local levels

Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) and Gauhati University have developed a new method to identify when the monsoon arrives at individual locations, distinguishing sustained monsoon rainfall from short-lived local showers.

The climate-network approach tracks how clusters of local rainfall onsets across India connect and evolve into a larger, interconnected monsoon system. The findings were published in the Journal of Climate, a peer-reviewed journal of the American Meteorological Society.

The researchers treated geographical locations as nodes in a climate network, with links representing spatial connections between locations experiencing local rainfall onset. By tracking the growth and movement of these clusters, the study offers an objective method to identify when local rainfall patterns become part of a larger, sustained monsoon system, rather than treating every spell of rain as the monsoon's onset.

The study was co-authored by Yogenraj Patil, Gaurav Chopra, Shruti Tandon and Professor R I Sujith from IIT Madras, and Professor B N Goswami of Gauhati University.

Paras Semiconductors partners with US-based BroadPak

Paras Semiconductors, a subsidiary of Paras Defence and Space Technologies, has entered into a strategic technology partnership with US-based BroadPak Corporation to strengthen India's advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities.

The collaboration will combine Paras Semiconductors' manufacturing ambitions in optoelectronics, photonics and co-packaged optics with BroadPak's expertise in advanced semiconductor packaging, heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based architectures. The partnership aims to establish an advanced heterogeneous integration and 3D packaging facility in India under the Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) model.

The proposed facility will focus on 2.5D and 3D packaging, chiplet integration, hybrid bonding, wafer-level and panel-level fan-out packaging, co-packaged optics, and advanced semiconductor testing and qualification. BroadPak, headquartered in San Jose, California, brings experience in packaging design, manufacturing and system integration, with capabilities spanning architecture, simulation, assembly, testing and production.

IIT Bhubaneswar study identifies silver iodide surface as potential host for stable electron spin

Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bhubaneswar have identified a specific surface of cubic zinc-blende silver iodide (AgI) as a promising candidate for hosting persistent spin texture (PST), a quantum phenomenon that could have applications in next-generation electronic devices.

The study, led by Dr Manish Kumar Mohanta, Ramanujan Faculty in the Department of Physics at IIT Bhubaneswar, has been published in Physical Review B, a journal of the American Physical Society. Persistent spin texture refers to the stable, unidirectional alignment of electron spins in certain nonmagnetic semiconductors. Since electrons possess an intrinsic property called spin, alongside their electric charge, this phenomenon could enable information to be processed and stored using electron spin.

The researchers note that persistent spin texture can suppress unwanted spin relaxation, allowing spin information to persist longer. This makes materials exhibiting the phenomenon promising candidates for spintronic devices, which use electron spin alongside electrical charge to process and store information.

(The copy will be updated with the latest news through the day)

item.title: Google Cloud India MD Shashikumar Sreedharan joins Sarvam as President and CBO
item.description: Sreedharan will run Sarvam's business across enterprises and government, and widen its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners.
item.content:encoded:
Sarvam, one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) startups in India, has announced the appointment of Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer. Sreeedharan was previously Managing Director - India of Google Cloud.

A blog post by Sarvam said Sreedharan will also be joining as a board member of the company. His responsibilities include leading the business of Sarvam across enterprises and government, and expanding its work with digital native companies, developers and partners. He will also be responsible for marketing, finance, forward deployed engineering, service delivery, and commercial operations.

“India should be a maker of the intelligence the world runs on. For me, joining Sarvam is a commitment to that opportunity. I look forward to working with the team and our customers to build products that become part of how industries and governments operate,” said Sreedharan.

Sreeedharan has more than three decades of experience building and leading technology businesses. Previously, he led Microsoft India’s enterprise business as the managing director for over five years.

Sarvam said the new appointment comes at a time when the startup is growing in scale and scope. It noted that over 100 enterprises and government institutions are building with Sarvam’s full-stack offering.

“The next phase of Sarvam is about advancing our research, developing products loved by people around the world, and building a company that can operate at a much greater scale. Every enterprise should own its AI,” the blog post said.

Sarvam became a unicorn startup after raising $234 million in the first close of its Series B funding round in June 2026. This round valued the company at $1.5 billion and saw participation from investors such as  HCLTech, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners.

item.title: Anthropic targets upto $1.4T valuation with $70 to $78 IPO price range
item.description: Anthropic will be valued at $1.41 trillion at the upper end of its IPO price band and the shares will be traded on Nasdaq.
item.content:encoded:
AI company Anthropic has set $70 to $78 as the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) which potentially values the company in the range of $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion.

The company will be offering 825 million shares. According to the filings, leading technology companies such as Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom will be purchasing $26 billion worth of shares in Anthropic through a private placement. Reports suggest that the company could raise in excess of $100 billion.

The report also said Anthropic will be pricing the shares of its IPO on November 18 and trade on November 19. The shares will be traded on Nasdaq stock exchange.

Anthropic, which has raised a total of $130 billion in funding, was last valued at $965 billion.

The AI company's valuation comes at a time when investors are questioning the valuation of AI companies. Anthropic, which was founded by Dario Amodei and others in 2021, was earlier seeking a valuation of $2 trillion. In comparison, the company reported revenue of $1.16 billion and losses of $12.96 billion in the first half of 2025.

Anthropic’s growth has been remarkable, with revenue rising from just $41 million in 2023 to $4.5 billion in 2025.

In its IPO filing, Anthropic said, “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history. If managed well, it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach and solve problems that have resisted generations of human efforts.”

“Anthropic aims to realise these while navigating and preventing the risks that come with a technological revolution this fast and this powerful.”

Anthropic believes the diffusion of AI through the global economy represents one of the largest opportunities in history to improve how humans live and work, and it is just beginning. It further noted that the world has only begun to use the capabilities of today’s frontier models, and the gap between what Claude can do and how broadly it is used represents one of our largest growth opportunities, alongside continued advances at the frontier.
